GIMME: Group Iterative Multiple Model Estimation

Source: R/gimme.R
build_gimme.Rd

build_gimme() estimates a directed network for each person from intensive longitudinal data with GIMME (group iterative multiple model estimation; Gates & Molenaar, 2012), in the unified structural equation model (uSEM): each variable at time \(t\) is regressed on the variables at \(t - 1\) (temporal, lagged paths) and on the other variables at \(t\) (contemporaneous paths). The search runs in two stages:

  1. Group-level paths: directed paths added for everyone because they would improve the model for a large share of the people (more than the share groupcutoff, by default 0.75, of the people whose models converged).

  2. Individual-level paths: further paths specific to each person, added after the group paths until that person's model fits well (see n_excellent).

It takes one long data frame with a person-ID column, not a directory of CSV files.

The temporal and contemporaneous count matrices say how many people have each path, which shows how common a path is in the sample, not how strong it is; the coefficients are estimated per person. Group paths are shared by construction, while individual paths are what the search adds for one person's series: before reading them, check each person's number of time points and fit statistics, which the result carries.

Usage

build_gimme(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  time = NULL,
  ar = TRUE,
  standardize = FALSE,
  groupcutoff = 0.75,
  subcutoff = 0.5,
  paths = NULL,
  exogenous = NULL,
  hybrid = FALSE,
  rmsea_cutoff = 0.05,
  srmr_cutoff = 0.05,
  nnfi_cutoff = 0.95,
  cfi_cutoff = 0.95,
  n_excellent = 2L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format: one row per person and time point, with the person-ID column, the variables and, optionally, a time or beep column.

vars

The names of the variables to model, at least two, all columns of data; a missing name raises an error.

id

The name of the person-ID column. The data must hold at least two people; a person with fewer than three time points is left out of the analysis without a warning.

time

The name of the time or order column. When given, the rows are sorted by id and then time before the lagged variables are formed; with NULL (default), the row order is used.

ar

Whether each variable's autoregressive path (itself at lag 1) is fixed into every model. Default TRUE.

standardize

Whether the variables are standardised within each person before estimation. Default FALSE. The coefficients come from lavaan's standardised solution either way, so this changes only the scale-dependent fit statistics (the log-likelihood, AIC and BIC); the chi-square, RMSEA, SRMR, NNFI and CFI do not change.

groupcutoff

A path is added at the group level when it is significant for more than this share of the people whose models converged, a number in (0, 1]. No group path is added when half or fewer of the models converge. Default 0.75.

subcutoff

Not used: reserved for subgrouping, which neither Nestimate nor idiographic::fit_gimme() implements, and accepted for compatibility with gimme; it is not passed on. Default 0.50.

paths

Paths, in lavaan syntax, to fix into every model, such as "V2~V1lag". Default NULL.

exogenous

The variables treated as exogenous (predictors only), all among vars; at least one variable must remain endogenous, and either rule broken raises an error. Default NULL.

hybrid

Whether the search also considers residual covariances between the variables at the same time point. Default FALSE.

rmsea_cutoff

The RMSEA at or below which a person's fit counts as excellent. Default 0.05.

srmr_cutoff

The SRMR at or below which a person's fit counts as excellent. Default 0.05.

nnfi_cutoff

The NNFI (TLI) at or above which a person's fit counts as excellent. Default 0.95.

cfi_cutoff

The CFI at or above which a person's fit counts as excellent. Default 0.95.

n_excellent

How many of the four fit indices must be excellent for a person's individual search to stop, a whole number from 1 to 4. Default 2.

seed

An integer that makes the estimation reproducible; the session's own random stream is left as it was. Default NULL.

Value

The net_gimme object (class c("net_gimme", "cograph_network", "list")) that idiographic::fit_gimme() returns; its print(), summary() and plot() methods are idiographic's, not Nestimate's. print() shows the group-level paths, the number of individual paths and the share of people with each path; summary() returns a data frame with one row per network layer (temporal, contemporaneous) and its size, density and weights; plot() draws the network. idiographic::edges() gives one row per path with its level (group or individual), and idiographic::coefs() one row per person and path with its coefficient. The object is a superset of the pre-0.9.0 in-package field contract: every field below is present, alongside idiographic's additions (contemp_cov, contemp_cov_avg, contemp_is_cov). Its fields:

temporal

p x p matrix of temporal (lagged) path counts: entry [i, j] is the number of people with the path j(t-1) -> i(t), group and individual paths alike.

contemporaneous

p x p matrix of contemporaneous path counts: entry [i, j] is the number of people with the path j(t) -> i(t).

temporal_avg, contemporaneous_avg

p x p group-average coefficient matrices.

coefs

List of per-person p x 2p coefficient matrices (rows the endogenous variables, columns the lagged and then the contemporaneous variables).

psi

List of per-person residual covariance matrices.

fit

Data frame of per-person fit indices (file, the person, then chisq, df, pvalue, rmsea, srmr, nnfi, cfi, bic, aic, logl and status).

path_counts

p x 2p matrix: how many people have each path.

paths

List of per-person character vectors of lavaan path syntax.

group_paths

Character vector of the group-level paths found.

individual_paths

List of per-person character vectors of the individual-level paths (beyond the group paths).

syntax

List of per-person full lavaan syntax strings.

labels

Character vector of variable names.

n_subjects

Number of people.

n_obs

Integer vector of the lagged time points per person (its rows minus one).

config

List of the settings used, including the corrections and cutoffs that are not arguments here.

The object also carries idiographic's network fields (nodes, edges, directed, data, meta, node_groups, and a weights entry that is NULL) for rendering with cograph.

Details

Estimation is delegated to idiographic::fit_gimme(), the clean-room home of the temporal idiographic estimators, whose search reproduces the upstream gimme package (>= 10.0) exactly (verified at tolerance 0 on path counts and per-person coefficient matrices in idiographic's own parity suite). The models are fitted with lavaan, which also gives the modification indices the search uses; build_gimme() raises an error when lavaan is not installed. The settings build_gimme() does not expose (such as the multiple-comparison corrections and alpha) keep idiographic::fit_gimme()'s defaults.

Results changed in 0.9.0

Before 0.9.0 the search ran in an in-package implementation that was not upstream-gimme-exact. Delegating to idiographic::fit_gimme() changed which paths the search selects on the same data – individual-level paths in particular – so numeric results are not comparable with Nestimate <= 0.8.5. The returned object also gained fields (see Value); nothing was removed.

References

Gates, K. M., & Molenaar, P. C. M. (2012). Group search algorithm recovers effective connectivity maps for individuals in homogeneous and heterogeneous samples. NeuroImage, 63(1), 310–319. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2012.06.026

See also

build_network

Examples

# \donttest{
# Create simple panel data (3 subjects, 4 variables, 30 time points).
set.seed(42)
n_sub <- 3; n_t <- 30; vars <- paste0("V", 1:4)
rows <- lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  d <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(n_t * 4), ncol = 4))
  names(d) <- vars; d$id <- i; d
})
panel <- do.call(rbind, rows)
res <- build_gimme(panel, vars = vars, id = "id")
print(res)
#> GIMME Network Analysis

#> Subjects:   3 
#> Variables:  4  ( V1, V2, V3, V4 )
#> AR paths:   yes 
#> Hybrid:     no 
#> 
#> Group-level paths found: 0 
#> 
#> Individual-level paths:  mean 0.3, range 0-1
#> 
#> Proportion of subjects with each path:
#> 
#>   Temporal [directed]
#>     weights [1.000, 1.000]  |  +4 / -0 edges
#>        V1 V2 V3 V4
#>     V1  1  0  0  0
#>     V2  0  1  0  0
#>     V3  0  0  1  0
#>     V4  0  0  0  1
#> 
#>   Contemporaneous [directed]

#>     V3  0  0  0 0.00

#>   plot(x)  (faithful gimme-style mixed network) | plot(x, layer = "temporal") 
#>   edges(x) | nodes(x) | summary(x) | coefs(x) | matrices(x)
